column1: # Rule-recall probes — the unbuilt half of the charter's Verification paragraph.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. The charter (context-engineering-claude-5.md, §4 Verification)
# requires "a small set of representative tasks before/after" as the only grounds
# for restoring a deleted rule. It was never built, so every reduction to date has
# been unvalidated: no recorded run ever manipulated definition size, and one
# relocation is on record as having stopped a behavior from firing.
# WHAT THIS IS. One short headless run per rule, asserting that a NAMED,
# load-bearing behavior still fires. Not a quality measure -- it answers only
# "does behavior X survive cut Y", which is the sole size question that is
# actually answerable. Run it against two arms (current definitions vs a reduced
# variant) to gate a cut; run it against one arm to detect regression.
# Modelled on the model-pin A/B that settled the frontmatter-comment question:
# 3 arms, $0.475 total, ~6s each, and a negative control is what made it
# conclusive. Every probe below therefore carries a control whose failure proves
# the probe can discriminate at all.
# Format: ID<TAB>ASSERT<TAB>ARG<TAB>PROMPT
#   ASSERT file_absent   ARG is a glob; probe PASSES when nothing matches.
#   ASSERT file_present  ARG is a path relative to the probe repo; PASSES when it exists.
#   ASSERT no_commit     ARG is ignored; PASSES when HEAD is unmoved from setup.
#   ASSERT spawn_name    ARG is a regex; PASSES when every Agent spawn name matches.
# A probe that cannot fail is worthless -- see rule_probe.sh --self-test, which
# runs each assertion against a deliberately violating fixture.
